narrative.overview: The dev.house mentors are working engineers who mentor after hours, and their students study around jobs and university. The interface is the desk they sit at in the evening: a dark graphite surface, everything in reach, nothing shouting. A single desk lamp, Signal Yellow, lights the one thing that needs you now. Density is a feature: ruled lists and tables with hairline dividers, figures in Geist Mono with tabular numerals. Depth comes from tone, not shadow. Motion is short and only reports state.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first graphite ground, tonal layering instead of shadows
One yellow signal per view; status is a tint, never a heavy fill
Ruled lists and tables over card grids
Geist for words, Geist Mono for every figure
Main column plus a quiet right-hand context rail
Flat, exact controls with hairline rings and visible focus

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Only one element per view is filled solid Signal Yellow: the next step. Every other use of yellow is text, a ring, or the Signal Yellow Ink tint.

rules.name: The Status-Is-A-Tint Rule
rules.body: Status is shown as a tinted background with matching text and a 1px inset ring, never as a solid fill.

rules.name: The Never-Colour-Alone Rule
rules.body: Every coloured status also carries a word or an icon, so meaning survives without colour.

rules.name: The Mono-For-Figures Rule
rules.body: If it is a number, a date or a duration, it is set in Geist Mono with tabular numerals. Mono is never used for prose or for technical decoration.

rules.name: The Small Section Rule
rules.body: Section headings are 14px semibold. Hierarchy comes from the content's own weight, not from big section titles.

rules.name: The Main-And-Rail Rule
rules.body: The main column holds what you act on; the rail holds context about who and when. New role homes follow the same split.

rules.name: The Tone-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: To lift something, move it one step up the graphite ladder and give it a hairline ring. Never add a drop shadow or glow.

dos: Do keep exactly one solid Signal Yellow element per view: the next step.
Do set every number, date and duration in Geist Mono with tabular numerals.
Do group items in one ruled list frame with hairline dividers.
Do pair every status colour with a word or icon.
Do turn time figures yellow only when they cross a real threshold (under 24h to a deadline, over 48h waiting).
Do use skeletons for loading and empty states that tell the user what to do next.
Do theme browser surfaces from the palette: yellow selection, caret and focus ring, graphite scrollbars.
donts: Don't build pages from grids of same-size cards with stock illustrations; this is not a course catalogue.
Don't add gamification: streaks, XP, badges, confetti.
Don't add drop shadows or glows; use the graphite ladder and hairline rings.
Don't put an eyebrow or kicker label above a heading.
Don't fill status pills solid; status is always a tint plus a ring.
Don't use Text Dimmed for anything a user must read.
Don't use Geist Mono for prose or as a "techy" costume.
Don't use a modal where an inline control works (course status, contest registration).
